title: Measures to Help in the Selling of HDB or Private Properties with Less than 60-year Leases
what_it_is: Measures to Help in the Selling of HDB or Private Properties with Less than 60-year Leases

sections.label: CPF flexibility and monetisation options
sections.summary: MND and CPF Board are working on more flexibility for using CPF monies to buy shorter-lease flats, and elderly owners have monetisation options including the Lease Buyback Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Ministry of National Development (MND) is also working with Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board on how we can provide more flexibility on the use of CPF monies to purchase flats with shorter leases while safeguarding retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are working out the details of these changes and will share them when ready.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Besides selling their HDB flats or private residential properties, elderly homeowners can consider other monetisation options to unlock the value of their properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: These options include renting out their spare bedrooms or the whole property or selling back part of their lease to HDB under the Lease Buyback Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As Members would be familiar, we have just recently announced the extension of the Lease Buyback Scheme to 5-room flats and larger HDB flats so that more Singaporeans can benefit from this scheme.

sections.label: Age and lease restrictions review
sections.summary: Restrictions require a minimum of 80 years for age and lease, flats with leases under 60 years face a proration formula, and the rules are being reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: First of all, one restriction is that your age and the lease of your flat must meet the minimum of 80 years, which is a point that the Member alluded to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Another restriction is that for a flat with a lease that is shorter than 60 years, there is a proration formula that kicks in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are reviewing these rules and, when ready, we will be able to share with the public what the revised rules are and the timeframe for when the new rules can be implemented, bearing in mind that, with CPF changes, it is not just about policy changes, but we also have to amend or update the information technology system for CPF.

sections.label: Lease Buyback Scheme expansion
sections.summary: The Lease Buyback Scheme lets those who wish to age in place stay in their flat, and it is being expanded to all HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Some may prefer to right-size and move out, but some may actually prefer to say, "I want to live in my present flat and age-in-place".

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Therefore, if that is your preference, we allow you an option, which is the Lease Buyback Scheme, and we are now expanding that option so that it is universal; so that it is not just confined to those staying in 4-room or smaller flats, but anyone in an HDB flat can have access to it.
